text:
maya: Quick thought — I'm exploring pushing RBAC evaluation out of the console projection layer and into the query-router. Reason: panels would only request filtered rows, reducing client-side logic and duplication. Tradeoffs: cache fragmentation vs simpler panel code. Thoughts?

jun: Curious, do you mean the router would add an `auth_mask` to the cache key and perform row-level filtering before returning? :thinking: That could explode cache space per-tenant.

eli: Yeah, +1 for consistency but watch memory. If we attach auth_mask to keys we lose cross-tenant cache reuse. Maybe we can use a two-stage cache: shared raw results + per-tenant filtered view on top.

maya: Exactly — two-stage cache idea. Raw result cached at query-signature, then small per-tenant projection cached separately. Panels request by `view_id` and `auth_token` -> router composes quickly.

sarah: We should be explicit about interface boundaries. Proposal for router API (pseudo-Go):

```go
// QueryRouter handles execution and optional auth projection.
type QueryRouter interface {
  Execute(ctx context.Context, q QueryRequest) (QueryResponse, error)
}

// QueryRequest contains the raw SQL/plan plus optional AuthMask.
type QueryRequest struct {
  Query   string
  Params  map[string]interface{}
  AuthMask *AuthMask // nil means caller will filter
}
```

If `AuthMask` provided, router guarantees rows are pre-filtered. Otherwise projection is caller responsibility.

jun: That signature looks clean. A couple of concerns: 1) auth evaluation cost — calculating row-level mask can be heavy for large responses, 2) SLO surface expands: router now needs to meet both query and auth SLOs.

eli: For (1) we can do lazy projection: if raw result size > threshold, return a cursor and stream projection; or return hints so client can do quick client-side short-circuit. For (2) agree — we need per-path SLOs and fallback. Router should be able to return `403-slim` placeholder rows when overloaded.

maya: Fallbacks are important. My mental migration plan:
- Phase 1: Add `AuthMask` parameter and make it optional. Panels keep sending nil. Router records metrics for mask evaluations.
- Phase 2: Pilot a few low-cardinality dashboards with AuthMask set. Measure cache hit, mem, p95/p99.
- Phase 3: If good, convert more dashboards and introduce two-stage cache.

sarah: Migration needs preflight flags and a toggle per-dashboard in Console. Also must update audit logs to show whether filtering happened in-router or client.

jun: Ops note: we should not change query signing scheme. Two-stage cache requires stable canonical query fingerprints. If caller parameters change (e.g., timezone), we still want raw cache hits.

eli: Implementation nit: AuthMask should be a compact bitmap or predicate ID — not a full policy blob. Router expands predicate ID against the policy service. Example message flow:
1) panel -> router: {query, params, predicate_id}
2) router fetches predicate rules from PolicyService (cached)
3) router applies projection or streams decisions

platform-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy of query-router v2 started for cluster `us-west-2` (canary=3 pods). Monitoring: router.auth_mask.latency, router.cache.hit_rate, router.mem.

maya: Good. Also need to think about RBAC auditing: if router filters, we must log which policy rule matched each row (or at least which rule set). Otherwise QA can't reproduce missing rows.

jun: Logging per-row is heavy. Log a summary: predicate_id + result_count + sample_row_keys (up to N). That should be enough for debugging.

eli: One more performance pattern: pre-compute projection columns on write for high-traffic tables. That reduces runtime filter cost. Might push some complexity to ingestion but huge wins on read SLOs.

maya: Agreed. OK next steps: I'll write a short RFC with the interface, migration plan, and the two-stage cache design. Want volunteers to review — @jun @eli @sarah? :thumbsup:

jun: I'll review.

eli: I can take the canary runbook and perf tests.

sarah: I'll own Console toggles & audit fields.

platform-bot: ticket created: PF-4821 "router-side RBAC projection RFC + canary" assigned to maya.

maya: Thanks — will share RFC today.

sarah: quick question — do we need to update docs for eval dashboards?

maya: Yes, add a migration note in docs and a tiny troubleshooting guide for missing rows.

jun: End-to-end tests we should add: 1) predicate changes invalidate per-tenant projection cache, 2) router fallback returns `403-slim` when projection fails, 3) raw cache hit unchanged for non-auth queries.

eli: I'll sketch tests.

maya: Perfect. Closing the thread for now, will ping when RFC link is up. :wave:
